description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of a multimodal misinformation detection model across two datasets — PHEME and PolitiFact — under various ablation conditions, as presented in the paper “Bridging Cognition and Emotion: Empathy-Driven Multimodal Misinformation Detection.” The vertical axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 75.0% to 95.0% in increments of 2.5%, while the horizontal axis lists six experimental conditions: “Ours” (the full model), “w/o comments,” “w/o text,” “w/o select,” “w/o emotion,” and “w/o cognition.” The chart is divided into two panels by a vertical dashed line: the left panel for PHEME and the right for PolitiFact. In PHEME, “Ours” achieves 89.84%, followed by “w/o comments” (86.82%), “w/o text” (80.10%), “w/o select” (88.80%), “w/o emotion” (87.34%), and “w/o cognition” (87.17%). In PolitiFact, “Ours” reaches 90.57%, followed by “w/o comments” (85.85%), “w/o text” (83.02%), “w/o select” (89.62%), “w/o emotion” (84.91%), and “w/o cognition” (87.74%). Each bar is color-coded: “Ours” in dark red, “w/o comments” in orange, “w/o text” in yellow, “w/o select” in light blue, “w/o emotion” in medium blue, and “w/o cognition” in dark blue. The results demonstrate that removing any component degrades performance, with “w/o text” causing the most significant drop in both datasets, underscoring the importance of textual features. The “Ours” model consistently outperforms all ablated variants, highlighting the effectiveness of integrating cognition, emotion, and multimodal selection mechanisms.
